title: What happens if you cry in space? 👀
subject: astronaut
description:
Could you keep working with one eye burning? 👇

Can you cry in space? Without gravity, tears don't run down your face; they pool on your eye. On a 2011 spacewalk, NASA astronaut Andrew Feustel found out the hard way when anti-fog soap got into his eye.

Sources: Space.com (May 27, 2011), NBC News ("Tears in Space Don't Run Down Your Face"), Associated Press via Phys.org (May 25, 2011)

why tears don't fall in space

scenes.text: Cry in space, and your tears won't fall.
Without gravity, the water clings to your eye and grows into a wobbling ball.
On May 25, 2011, Andrew Feustel was on a spacewalk outside the International Space Station.
Anti-fog soap from inside his helmet got into his right eye.
He radioed: "My right eye is stinging like crazy right now. It's watering a lot."
He rubbed it on a foam pad inside his helmet. "Tears in space don't run down your face," he said later.
